briefing.text: The library reports that data_clinical_patient.txt holds only PATIENT_ID, CENTER, STAGE and SEX for 101 patients, with no OS_MONTHS, OS_STATUS or other survival column. Confirm this by searching the headers of every clinical file for OS_, DFS_, SURVIVAL and VITAL. Under this task's labelling convention, a missing survival variable does not by itself make the hypothesis 'Not verifiable'. This hypothesis is about this study's cancer (gallbladder) and a gene on its panel (SMAD4 is on IMPACT410), so the label must be True or False. Use the closest variables the tables hold, together with the study context and established biology, and say which kind of evidence decided the label.
briefing.reason: Without this, a team that finds no survival column could pick 'Not verifiable', which the convention marks wrong for a hypothesis about this study.

briefing.text: Define SMAD4 alteration carefully. Homozygous deletions (value -2 for SMAD4 in data_cna.txt) and disruptive structural variants (data_sv.txt) are major ways SMAD4 is inactivated in biliary cancer, so count them alongside mutations. Limit mutations to non-synonymous, likely damaging variants such as truncations and hotspots like R361. Samples with SOMATIC_STATUS=Unmatched may contain germline calls. Report results under two definitions: mutation only, and mutation or deep deletion or SV.
briefing.reason: The definition of SMAD4-altered sets the size of the comparison groups and can change the direction of any proxy comparison.

briefing.text: data_clinical_sample.txt lists 103 samples for about 101 patients. Some patients have more than one sample, mixing primary and metastasis, and two sample-ID schemes are in use (s_WJ_gb_* and P-000*). Map each SAMPLE_ID to its PATIENT_ID through data_clinical_sample.txt, then collapse to one SMAD4 status per patient (altered if any sample is altered) before comparing groups or joining to the patient table.
briefing.reason: Analysing per sample double-counts patients and can join rows to the wrong patient, which biases group comparisons such as SMAD4 against stage.

briefing.text: With about 100 patients and only 10-20% SMAD4-altered, any outcome or proxy test has low power. A p-value above 0.05 is not evidence against a worse-outcome claim. Report how many patients are altered, the event counts, and the effect size with its 95% CI, and read the direction of the effect rather than the p-value alone. Picking the most significant of many genes or definitions inflates false positives.
briefing.reason: This stops the team from labelling the hypothesis False only because a small-sample test was not significant.

shared_assumptions: Both teams assume that stage IV vs <IV (and metastatic sample type) is a valid stand-in for overall survival, and that a non-significant enrichment in the expected direction counts as support rather than as absence of evidence.

Both teams assume that 'the label follows the source study's likely finding' means a prognostic SMAD4 effect, without testing whether the in-data proxy direction would also be consistent with a reversed or null claim.

Both assume every non-synonymous SMAD4 call (including missense of unknown significance) is a functional mutation, and that patients are independent across three centers (USA, Chile, Japan) and two sample series (s_WJ research and P- clinical IMPACT samples).
Both treat missing stage/center (20 patients) as ignorable, i.e. missing at random.
unused_evidence: Hotspot, t_alt_count/t_depth and Mutation_Status/exac_filter columns in the mutation table: never used to separate likely-functional SMAD4 variants from passenger missense calls.

TUMOR_PURITY, SAMPLE_COVERAGE and SOMATIC_STATUS (3 Unmatched samples) in the sample table: low purity can hide SMAD4 deep deletions and unmatched samples can carry germline calls; neither team reported checking these for SMAD4-defining samples.
TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS and GENE_PANEL (IMPACT341 vs IMPACT410): hypermutated samples or panel differences could inflate the SMAD4-mutant group.
The Japan center (11 staged patients) is present in the patient table, but team A reported strata only for USA and Chile.
The 20 patients with blank STAGE/CENTER appear to be one distinct sample series (P- clinical IMPACT IDs); they are excluded from the stage proxy without examining their SMAD4 rate.
unresolved_weak_points: Both teams named the lack of survival data and the reliance on prior biology as the weakest point; neither resolved it, they only reported it.
Team B flagged that the source study could have reported no association (making the label False) and kept True without any check that discriminates the two.
Team B flagged SMAD4 concentration in gallstone-present and Chilean patients as a possible confounder of the stage proxy, but did not adjust for it.
Team A's numbers differ between its memory records (stage IV 14/27=52%, p=0.11) and its submitted note (67% vs 43%, OR 2.64, p=0.08); the denominator in use is unclear.
second_readings: 'SMAD4 mutations' may mean point mutations only, not mutation-or-deep-deletion; the two definitions can give different directions.
'Worse overall survival' is a time-to-event claim; a stage-distribution difference is a different quantity (association with advanced disease, not survival conditional on stage).
'Gallbladder cancer patients' could mean the full cohort or a single center/series; the label could depend on which cohort the source finding was made in.
challenge.verdict: Moderate-to-low trust: the shared True rests on prior biology and a weak, non-significant stage proxy, with no survival data and an unresolved possibility that the source finding was null. The data cannot test the claim directly, so the label depends mostly on the benchmark convention rather than on analysis.

questions.question: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Your memory records stage IV 14/27=52% (p=0.11) but your method note reports 67% vs 43% (OR 2.64, p=0.08). Re-run the SMAD4 vs stage IV table once with an explicit patient denominator and alteration definition; which is correct, and does the corrected figure change how much weight the proxy gets?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: The patient table has a Japan center (11 staged patients) that your stratified analysis does not mention. Does adding the Japan stratum (e.g. Mantel-Haenszel across all three centers) keep the direction of the SMAD4-stage IV association, and does that change your method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Restrict SMAD4 mutations to truncating or Hotspot-flagged calls, excluding samples with SOMATIC_STATUS Unmatched and very high TMB. Does the stage IV enrichment survive with that stricter definition, and does the result change your method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: The 20 patients with blank STAGE/CENTER seem to form a separate sample series. What is their SMAD4 alteration rate and sample-type mix compared with the staged patients, and does excluding them bias the proxy comparison?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: You flagged gallstones and Chile as possible confounders. Run the SMAD4 vs stage IV comparison stratified by center and by GALLBLADDER_STONES (or a logistic model with both). Does the direction hold within strata, and does that change your method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: You named a null source finding (label False) as a live possibility. What in-data check would separate 'True' from 'False' here, e.g. whether the SMAD4 effect on stage is no larger than that of other common GBC genes (TP53, ERBB2, ARID1A) under the same test? Does running it change your method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Check TUMOR_PURITY and SAMPLE_COVERAGE for SMAD4 wild-type samples. Are low-purity samples, where a deep deletion could be missed, concentrated in one stage group, and does excluding them change the stage IV comparison?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Your stage proxy is positive (p=0.13) but the metastatic-sample proxy is null (p=0.79). Restrict to Primary samples only, one per patient, and recheck SMAD4 vs stage IV. Do the two proxies then agree, and does that change your method?

questions.why: Both teams' label leans on stage as a stand-in for overall survival; whether that surrogate is accepted decides how much the proxy can count.

questions.question: What is the published consensus on SMAD4 alteration as an independent prognostic factor for overall survival in gallbladder or biliary tract cancer, and do studies differ on whether the effect remains after adjustment for stage?
questions.why: Both teams fall back on 'established biology'; if the literature is mixed or null after adjustment, the fallback does not support True by default.

questions.why: The SMAD4-mutant group includes many missense calls; the alteration definition can shift the comparison.

findings.question: In cancer-genomics survival analyses, how strongly does tumour stage at diagnosis predict overall survival in gallbladder cancer, and is stage IV commonly accepted as a surrogate for survival when time-to-event data are missing?
findings.answer: The web did not settle this: the research gateway returned HTTP 403 on every search and contents call, so no page was read. From background knowledge only: AJCC stage is the strongest established prognostic factor in gallbladder cancer. 5-year OS falls from above 50% in stage I to under 5% in stage IV, and median OS in stage IV is under about 12 months. Stage IV is not a formally accepted surrogate endpoint for OS, so a stage-based proxy is indirect, weak evidence. It should not be presented as a survival test.

findings.question: When annotating targeted-panel mutation data, which SMAD4 missense variants are conventionally treated as oncogenic (e.g. MH2-domain hotspots) versus variants of unknown significance?
findings.answer:
The web did not settle this: the research gateway returned HTTP 403, so no page was read. From background knowledge only, these count as oncogenic or likely oncogenic under OncoKB/cBioPortal conventions:
- SMAD4 truncating variants (nonsense, frameshift, splice-site)
- homozygous deletions
- recurrent missense hotspots, mainly in the MH2 domain (about aa 323-552): R361 (C/H/S/P), D351, D355, P356, G386, R496, D537, plus some MH1 residues such as R100
Other missense calls without hotspot or functional evidence are usually VUS. Report the SMAD4 group both with and without VUS missense calls.
